Origin & botanical facts
Snap beans, like kidney beans, white
beans, pinto beans, and cranberry beans,
are members of the common bean species,
all of which trace their origins to the

both whole and prechopped.  Fresh snap
beans can be steamed or simmered until
the pods are tender.  Steaming is the
preferred method of cooking because it
preserves nutrients.  Chopped into 1- or
2-inch sections, snap beans can be tossed
in salads, stir-fried, included in soups and
stews, or served as a side dish. 
Nutrient composition
Yellow and green snap beans are a good
source of vitamin C.
